caseStudy.problem: I needed a small portfolio that could present my engineering background and accept contact messages without running a traditional application server.
work: Built the responsive interface with React, TypeScript, and CSS Modules.
Kept portfolio content in repository-managed JSON files.
Connected the contact form to an AWS serverless email flow.
decisions: Use GitHub Pages for static hosting and a custom domain.
Separate content from components so factual updates do not require layout changes.
Use API Gateway, Lambda, and SES for contact delivery instead of maintaining a dedicated backend.
caseStudy.impact: The site remains a static deployment while still providing a direct contact path. Portfolio content stays versioned alongside the code.

caseStudy.problem: Long technical knowledge-transfer recordings were difficult to search and reuse, especially when they contained project-specific terminology and multiple speakers.
work: Built a local-first Python transcription pipeline using faster-whisper with the large-v3 model.
Added technical hotwords, optional speaker diarization with pyannote, and conservative speaker smoothing for cleaner transcripts.
Containerized the workflow with Docker for Windows with NVIDIA GPU acceleration and macOS CPU execution.
decisions: Keep transcription local instead of sending recordings to an external transcription API.
Keep the clean Whisper transcript separate from the speaker-aware version while preserving JSON as the canonical structured output.
caseStudy.impact: Successfully tested the pipeline on multiple real technical KT recordings, producing reusable Markdown, JSON, TXT, SRT, and VTT outputs with optional speaker attribution.

caseStudy.problem: This final-year project explored operational problems in Lisbon's Tuk Tuk sector, including inconsistent pricing and coordination between tourists, drivers, and companies.
work: Developed separate frontend applications for tourists and professional users.
Built the mobile interfaces with Angular and Ionic.
Hosted both applications on AWS and automated deployments from repository changes.
decisions: Separate the tourist and professional workflows instead of forcing both audiences into one interface.
Use Angular and Ionic to share a cross-platform frontend approach.
Automate deployment on code changes so both applications followed the same delivery process.
caseStudy.impact: Delivered both frontend applications as the project implementation and received a final grade of 15/20.
